The DeBERTa model, integrated into GordonAI, specializes in sentiment analysis, emotion detection, and fact-checking classification in multiple languages. It is based on the mdeberta-v3-base model fine-tuned on a fact-checking dataset to categorize text into Disinformation, Hoax, FakeNews, or TrueNews classes. DeBERTa's architecture features disentangled attention and an enhanced mask decoder, surpassing human performance on SuperGLUE benchmarks and excelling in Natural Language Understanding (NLU) and Natural Language Generation (NLG) tasks.

The disentangled attention mechanism in DeBERTa improves performance by computing attention weights based on content and relative positions, enhancing various Natural Language Processing (NLP) tasks. By incorporating absolute word positions in the mask decoder, DeBERTa enhances predictions during masked language modeling tasks. Its Transformer-based design with stacked Transformer blocks and disentangled attention mechanism enables superior performance in fact-checking, sentiment analysis, and emotion detection tasks across diverse languages.

Additionally, the Scale-Invariant Fine-Tuning (SiFT) algorithm enhances training stability by perturbing normalized word embeddings, leading to improved performance, especially in larger DeBERTa models. SiFT normalizes word embedding vectors into stochastic vectors before perturbation, significantly benefiting the fine-tuned models' performance, particularly in downstream NLP tasks. The model's Enhanced Mask Decoder (EMD) incorporates absolute word positions after Transformer layers, enhancing performance compared to early incorporation methods like BERT. SiFT's normalization of word embeddings enhances training stability, particularly beneficial for larger DeBERTa models, improving overall model performance.

It is important to note that SiFT is specifically applied to DeBERTa15B for SuperGLUE tasks in the experiments conducted, with a promise of a more comprehensive study of SiFT in future work.
